claims.claim: Register letters: L = 16' bassoon rank (one octave below written pitch), M = 8' clarinet rank (unison), H = 4' piccolo rank (one octave above). Common combinations: LM Bandoneon, MH Oboe, LH Organ, LMH Harmonium, MM(-) Violin, MMH Musette (M, M-, M+ with H as listed by some sources), LMM(-) Accordion, all ranks Master. Sources disagree on Master (LMM-M+ versus all voices) and some makers use different names, so the mapping is not standardised.

claims.claim: The input file's '448 reeds' arithmetic (328 treble plus 120 bass) cannot be traced to a source and looks wrong: reed counts depend on the model. A 120-bass left hand with 5 ranks would have 5 x 96 (or similar) tongues rather than 120; the '120 bass reed tongues' figure conflates 120 buttons with reeds.

claims.claim: Cottingham's work on free-reed transients (Vienna Talk 2015 with Wolff; ISMA 2017 paper 52) found that reed onset begins with irregular motion, then a short transition, then amplitude growth; second transverse and first torsional tongue modes appear in the transient, the torsional mode being important in larger, lower reeds. Curving the tongue may ease the slow speech of large low reeds. No numerical onset times were found.

summary: First pass only: 25 claims, all from search extracts because every fetch host was blocked. The 2021 Acoustics in Practice pitch-bend study exists (Elejalde-Garcia et al.) and the 15 and 25 cent figures match its abstract; the even/odd statement is only partly traceable. Ricot, Causse and Misdariis 2005 exists as a JASA abstract with a different title from the file's description. Register letters are broadly right but sources disagree on Master. Accordion plates are mostly aluminium with steel tongues, not brass or phosphor bronze. The melodica soprano range F4 to F6 is refuted for common models (P-37D is F3 to F6). Cassotto frequency band, 448 reeds, A7 and G1 figures, the 10 kHz spectrum, attack times and most melodica construction claims are untraced. Needs a second pass with fetch access.
